newsitem.title: CANADA: St. Lawrence Seaway 1996 cargo down 0.4 pct vs '95.
newsitem.headline: St. Lawrence Seaway 1996 cargo down 0.4 pct vs '95.

text.p: Overall cargo volumes through Canada's St. Lawrence Seaway were down 0.4 percent in the 1996 shipping season up to Oct 31 compared with the previous year, the St. Lawrence Seaway Authority said in a statement.
There were, however, increases in movements of iron ore, coal, stone, salt, sugar, coke, steel products and imported steel slabs.

Grain shipments fell 22.9 percent to 9.16 million tonnes from 11.879 million tonnes in the same period in the 1995 shipping season due to limited supplies from the 1995/96 (Aug/July) Canadian and America harvests, the statement said.

"The outlook for the remainder of the season is promising and overall traffic results on the St. Lawrence Seaway may equal or even surpass last year's results," St. Lawrence Seaway Authority president Glen Stewart said in the release.
Western Canada recorded its largest harvest of its six major grains and oilseeds this autumn, Statistics Canada and Canadian Wheat Board figures show.
Seaway revenues were higher than in the same period the previous year, the statement said.
